## 📊 Dataset Initial Work

The complete dataset is now imported into GitHub in `DataAccessFile.Rmd`. To fully understand the dataset and make sure it is ready for model fitting, we need to complete the following work.

### 1. Document each variable

For every column (characteristic / parameter):

- [ ] Identify the column and its corresponding characteristic, and write a **description**
- [ ] Mark whether it is **categorical** or **quantitative**
  - If categorical, list all categories with their associated meanings
- [ ] Annotate the **constraints and specifications** given by the data collection process
- [ ] Find and note the **number of N/A values**

### 2. Clean the dataset

- [ ] Remove the **first three rows**. They are descriptive, not actual observations.
- [ ] Remove the **first column**. It is not a characteristic.
- [ ] Remove observations with missing data **only when that column is needed** as a parameter for a particular question.

### 3. Combine time-separated columns

Earnings and employment columns are split by years since service, so we need to decide which to use for each question.

| Mutation | Description |
|----|----|
| **Earnings** | Combine the earnings columns and take the **mean** |
| **Employment status** | Combine the employment status columns and take the **mean** |

### 4. Split the data

- [ ] Split into **training / testing sets at 70 / 30**

### 5. Explore

Once the above is done, create scatter plots and other plot types to get initial ideas of which models are appropriate to start fitting.

## ❓ Project Questions

**What questions would we like to answer from this dataset? Are they feasible to answer?**

We need to look at each question separately and determine whether our dataset allows us to answer it. After this analysis we choose which questions to move forward with.

### For each question, identify:

| \# | Consideration |
|----|----|
| 1 | What is the **response variable**? |
| 2 | Do we need **regression** or **classification**? |
| 3 | Is the question **amenable** to the parameters in this dataset? |
| 4 | What **nuances in how the parameters were gathered** are important to consider? |
| 5 | Based on how the data was collected, how do we need to **adjust the interpretive statements** we make from our models? |

## 🧪 Model Fitting Expectations

### General rules

| Setting | Value |
|----|----|
| **Seed** | `445` |
| **Train / test split** | 70 / 30 for all models, so testing metrics are comparable across models |
| **Cross-validation** | 10-fold CV on the training data wherever possible |
| **Model type** | Use only models appropriate for the response variable (regression vs. classification) |

For each question, fit the models below and compute **all appropriate testing metrics** for each, so we can compare which fits best.

> 📈 **Every model fit must be accompanied by a representative plot.**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 📉 Regression

**Metric:** Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) through 10-fold CV

| Model | Requirements | Metric |
|----|----|----|
| **Tree** | One tree fit with a bagging, random forest, or boosting extension | CV RMSE |
| **KNN** | One KNN model | CV RMSE |
| **Stepwise selection** | Forward and backward. Test with Cp, AIC, BIC, Adj R², and CV | Cp / AIC / BIC / Adj R² / CV |
| **Shrinkage** (at least one) | Ridge **or** Lasso | CV RMSE, λ selected with `lambda.min` |
| **Dimension reduction** (at least one) | PCA **or** PLS | CV RMSE, with the optimal number of components *K* chosen |
| **Linear / quasi-linear** (at least one, if appropriate) | e.g. 3rd-degree polynomial splines, **GAM** | CV RMSE |

> Within linear models, we need stepwise selection, at least one shrinkage method, and at least one dimension reduction method.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 🏷️ Classification

**Metric:** Testing error rate (10-fold CV), with **confusion matrices attached** and **accuracy percentage**

| Model                      | Requirements   |
|----------------------------|----------------|
| **Logistic Regression**    | At least 1     |
| **LDA or QDA**             | One of the two |
| **Support Vector Machine** | One SVM        |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### ✅ Quick checklist per model

- [ ] Correct model type for the response (regression or classification)
- [ ] Seed `445` set
- [ ] 70/30 split used
- [ ] 10-fold CV on training data
- [ ] All appropriate test metrics recorded
- [ ] Representative plot included
